  "text": "He had wanted to know whether things stayed buried.

Every afternoon afterward, he had dug it up. On the fourth day the notches were gone. He made them again, deeper, and told nobody.

Now he rubbed his thumb across them.

“Which tree?” he asked.

The man glanced at the woman.

“We looked under all of them.”

“There was only one.”

For a moment the house was quiet enough for him to hear Anne breathing against the cupboard door.

Then the man smiled.

“You were smaller then.”

His father said that too. Usually when the boy remembered something differently: a room, a holiday, the height of a wall. He had never thought it might be a way of taking things away.

The woman lifted her shoe. The broken stone lay in two pieces. Inside was a small hollow lined with something soft and yellow.

“There's still time,” she told the man.

Anne's fingers tightened.

The boy turned the key toward the cupboard lock.

“Not that door,” she said.

He stopped.

Through the gap he could see one of her eyes. He had been avoiding it, grateful for her voice and unwilling to look too closely at anything else.

“Then let go.”

She did not.

The man took a step backward. That frightened the boy more than his coming nearer would have done.

“Anne,” the woman said, very softly. “Give him his sleeve.”

The fingers opened one at a time.

Behind the coats, where the plaster had always bulged in winter, something clicked.

The boy carried the key toward it. None of them asked where he was going."
